extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, IP litigators, patent applicants, and other readers interested in Federal Circuit patent case trends
extracted.subtask_short: empirical review of Federal Circuit decisions
extracted.subtask_description: An empirical summary and year-over-year comparison of all Federal Circuit patent decisions in calendar year 2022, reporting counts, outcome rates, and trends (precedentialness, dissents, eligibility outcomes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Federal Circuit patent cases decided
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Circuit decided far fewer patent cases in 2022 than in previous years — over 100 less than in 2021, which was itself a down year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report raw case counts for the year and compare to prior years to identify changes in docket volume; use absolute and percentage change to contextualize significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmance rate (overall and by origin)
rubrics_metrics.description: The court's affirmance rate in 2021 was also much lower than normal. That was primarily due to a stunningly low affirmance rate in district court cases — just 57%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure affirmance rates overall and disaggregate by source of appeal (e.g., district court appeals vs PTAB appeals). Compare year-over-year to spot shifts in affirmance behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentee/applicant success by appeal source
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentees and patent applicants fared much better than in 2021 in district court appeals, worse in appeals from the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, and about the same overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break out outcomes (wins/losses, reversals/affirmances) separately for appeals originating from district courts and from the PTAB to assess where patentees are gaining or losing ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedential decision rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of precedential decisions increased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track the proportion of decisions designated precedential versus nonprecedential or summary affirmances to understand shifts in the court's use of precedential opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissent rate
rubrics_metrics.description: But so did the dissent rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure frequency and proportion of opinions that include dissents (or concurrences/dissents) as an indicator of inter-judge disagreement and doctrinal division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent eligibility (§101) outcomes/trend
rubrics_metrics.description: The court was not quite as draconian in patent eligibility cases, but patentees and applicants still struggled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze §101/patent-eligibility decisions separately, reporting reversal/affirmance rates and comparing severity to prior years to evaluate patentee prospects on eligibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology: inclusion of all decision types
rubrics_metrics.description: This year's study covers all patent cases decided by the Federal Circuit in 2022, whether by precedential opinion, nonprecedential opinion or summary affirmance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compiling datasets or reporting statistics, include precedential opinions, nonprecedential opinions, and summary affirmances to reflect the full universe of decided patent cases for the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-over-year comparative context
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparisons to 2021 (and implicitly earlier years) are used to contextualize 2022 outcomes (e.g., over 100 fewer cases than 2021; 2021 had anomalously low affirmance rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always present trends with baseline comparisons to prior year(s) to indicate whether observed metrics reflect anomalies or part of multi-year trends.
